title: Sequential extraction procedure to obtain the composition of terrigenous detritus in marine sediments
author: Simon, Babin, et al.

steps.title: Weigh and Disaggregate Sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 2–3 g of the sediment into a dry, tared 50 mL centrifuge tube and record the mass. Weigh a clean, labeled 63 µm sieve for each sample and record its mass. Add deionized water to the tube to a total volume of approximately 30 mL, then vortex and/or sonicate to achieve good disaggregation (the better the disaggregation, the less water needed later).

steps.title: Sieving and Collecting Fractions
steps.instruction: Place a labeled 63 µm sieve in a 400 mL beaker, pour the sample onto the sieve, and use a squirt bottle with deionized water to transfer the entire sample. Wash the fine fraction through the sieve with the spray bottle until the outflow water is clear and the coarse fraction shows no clumps under a microscope. Transfer the coarse fraction to a pre‑weighed 63 µm sieve, dry it in an oven at 50 °C, and weigh the dry coarse fraction; store it in a small glass vial. Allow the fine fraction to settle in the beaker overnight; if still cloudy, add a few drops of the buffered 1 M acetic acid (see Step 4) to aid settling. After settling, decant as much water as possible, recombine beakers if needed, and return the fine fraction to the original 50 mL centrifuge tube. If necessary, fill the tube to 50 mL, centrifuge 30 min at 2400 rpm, decant, add remaining water and fine fraction, and centrifuge/decant again.

steps.title: Remove Organic Matter with H₂O₂
steps.instruction: Place each fine‑fraction sample in a beaker and add 50–100 mL of dilute 3 % hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂). Stir with a glass rod to suspend the sample, rinsing the rod between samples and drying it with lab tissue. When bubbling slows or stops, add another 50–100 mL of dilute H₂O₂ and restir. The step may be performed at 60–70 °C in a hot water bath, and the H₂O₂ concentration may be increased to ~6 % for high organic‑matter samples. When addition of H₂O₂ no longer produces bubbles, organics are removed. Allow the suspension to settle, then carefully siphon or pour off the supernatant, or wash the sample by centrifugation.

steps.title: Decarbonate Sediment with Buffered Acetic Acid
steps.instruction: Vortex the sample to loosen it, then add deionized water and 1 M buffered acetic acid to bring the tube volume to ~30 mL. Release any CO₂ produced. Vortex again to fully disaggregate, reseal the caps tightly, and place the tube on a rocking table for 6–12 h (or overnight). Centrifuge 30 min at 2400 rpm and decant the clear acid solution to waste. Repeat the entire sequence (add acid, vortex, rock, centrifuge, decant) until no further CO₂ evolution or bubbling is observed, indicating complete removal of carbonates.

steps.title: Leach Fe‑Mn Oxyhydroxide Fraction (pH ≈ 4)
steps.instruction: Fill each tube to ~20 mL with the buffered acetic acid/sodium acetate solution (pH ≈ 4) and place on a rocking table for at least 8 h (or overnight). Centrifuge 30 min at 2400 rpm and decant the clear supernatant. If the supernatant is colorless, stop; if tinted, repeat the leach until the supernatant is clear. After the final leach, add ~30 mL of MQ water, vortex to disaggregate, centrifuge 30 min at 2400 rpm and decant. Repeat the entire Step 5 (acid leach, rinse, centrifuge) two additional times. If settling becomes difficult after acid removal, increase centrifuge speed and/or time as needed.

steps.title: Settle Clay Fraction (<2 µm)
steps.instruction: Label clean 100 mL graduated cylinders with sample names and place a piece of tape 5 cm below the 100 mL mark. Label matching centrifuge tubes for the <2 µm fraction. Add ~30 mL MQ water and ~2 mL 0.5 % sodium metaphosphate (Calgon; NaPO₃)₆ (Fischer Chemical, Cat # S333‑500) to each tube after the third MQ rinse, vortex to disaggregate, and pour the contents into the corresponding cylinder, using a squirt bottle to transfer all sediment. Fill each cylinder to the 100 mL mark, cover with parafilm, sonicate for ~5 min, then shake and invert several times to ensure complete dispersion. Place cylinders on a stable surface and start a timer for 3 h 52 min (avoid disturbance). After the timer, use a turkey baster to withdraw the top 5 cm of water (≈25 mL) into the pre‑labeled centrifuge tubes (this contains the <2 µm fraction). For a second settling round, add ~2 mL Calgon to each cylinder, refill to 100 mL with MQ water, cover, sonicate 5 min, shake, and reset the timer. Centrifuge the collected tubes at 4000 rpm for 30 min; the supernatant should be translucent (it may be tinted). If still cloudy, repeat centrifugation for a longer period. Repeat the transfer (step 8) and centrifugation (step 10) cycles until the <2 µm fraction is sufficiently settled or enough material has been collected. Verify clarity by holding a black‑and‑white printed sheet up to the supernatant; sharp contrast indicates clarity. Transfer the remaining 2–63 µm fraction back to the original centrifuge tubes (or to clean tubes) using the MQ squirt bottle, then centrifuge 30 min, decant, and repeat until the cylinder is empty. Note any residual <2 µm material on the tubes.

steps.title: CsCl Cation‑Exchange Wash
steps.instruction: Fill each 50 mL centrifuge tube to the 15 mL line with MQ water. Label new 15 mL centrifuge tubes with the sample name plus “w/ CsCl”. Vortex the 50 mL tube to fully disaggregate, then quickly pipette 5 mL of the suspension into the 15 mL tube while the sample is still fully suspended. Rinse the pipette tip by drawing 5 mL MQ water into the 15 mL tube twice, then discard 5 mL MQ water into waste three times to clean the tip. Repeat the vortex‑transfer‑rinse sequence for the remaining sample, using fresh MQ water each time. Centrifuge all 15 mL tubes for 90 min at 4000 rpm and carefully pipette off the supernatant (do not pour). Add 10 mL of 0.1 N CsCl solution (INDOFINE, Research Grade, F.W. = 168.36, Cat # MB1006) to each tube, vortex to fully suspend (sonication may be required). Rotate the tubes on a rocker for 24 h to allow ion exchange. Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 20 min, then decant the liquid without loss of sediment. Add 10 mL MQ water, vortex, centrifuge 20 min at 2000 rpm, and decant; repeat this wash once more. Add 10 mL ethanol (C₂H₆O, denatured, Fisher Chemical, Cat # A407‑500), vortex, centrifuge 20 min at 2000 rpm, and decant; repeat the ethanol wash a second time. Finally, dry the samples in an oven at 50 °C (freeze‑drying is unsuitable because of ethanol’s low freezing point).
